headline: Uber Cuts Contract Review Time 20% with Rules-Based + RAG Legal AI Agent
summary: Uber built an internal legal AI agent that automates contract redlining by combining deterministic rule engines with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). The hybrid approach lets the system apply hard legal/compliance rules precisely while using RAG to pull relevant contract clauses and precedent language, cutting legal contract review time by 20% without sacrificing accuracy.
why_it_matters: This is a strong real-world example of combining RAG with rule-based logic to build reliable enterprise agents—directly relevant to your work building LLM applications on ServiceNow, where similar hybrid patterns (deterministic workflow logic + generative retrieval) are key to production-grade AI agents.

headline: Meta's JiTTests: LLM-Generated Tests That Try to Break Risky Code Before It Ships
summary: Meta introduced JiTTests, a system that uses LLMs to generate 'just-in-time' tests specifically designed to fail on risky or privacy-sensitive code changes before they're merged. The approach targets catching subtle bugs (like privacy violations) that traditional test suites often miss, by having the LLM reason about what could go wrong with a given diff and writing adversarial tests accordingly.
why_it_matters: As LLM-driven development tooling matures, this shows how generative AI can be applied to software quality and safety gates—useful context for engineering robust AI-assisted development pipelines and for thinking about how to harden your own LLM application code against edge cases.

headline: Hark Ships Handoff², a 2x Faster Computer-Use Agent
summary: Hark released Handoff², an updated computer-use agent for its Hark Pro platform that doubles the speed of prior agent interactions with desktop/GUI environments, improving task completion latency for automated computer-use workflows.
why_it_matters: Computer-use agents are becoming a core building block for automating enterprise workflows (similar to ServiceNow automation use cases); tracking performance gains in this space helps you benchmark and evaluate tooling options for agentic automation projects.

headline: Governed Autonomous Intelligence: Designing AI for Mission-Critical Utility Systems
summary: This article explores architectural patterns for deploying autonomous AI agents in mission-critical utility (energy/infrastructure) settings, emphasizing governance frameworks, guardrails, and human oversight mechanisms needed to safely operate AI in high-stakes environments.
why_it_matters: Governance and guardrail design are increasingly central to enterprise AI engineering roles, including ServiceNow-based AI workflows; understanding how mission-critical industries structure autonomy and oversight can inform best practices for your own agent deployments.

headline: AWS Open-Sources Local Emulator for 200+ Services to Support Coding Agents
summary: AWS has open-sourced an emulator that replicates over 200 AWS services locally, enabling coding agents and developers to test cloud-dependent code without deploying to live AWS infrastructure, speeding up iteration and reducing cost/risk during agentic coding workflows.
why_it_matters: This lowers the barrier for safely testing AI coding agents against realistic cloud environments—valuable if you're building or evaluating agentic coding tools, and relevant to local/sandboxed testing patterns you might apply when developing ServiceNow or LLM-integrated applications.
